newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-WAUGH AND BLEWETT REWRITE RECORD BOOKS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH AND BLEWETT REWRITE RECORD BOOKS.

text.p: Record breakers Steve Waugh and Greg Blewett continued to make South Africa suffer on the fourth morning of the first test at the Wanderers as Australia reached 574 for five at lunch, a lead of 272.

Overnight Australia were 479 for four, with Blewett on 156 and Waugh on 137, the pair having batted throughout the third day. When Jacques Kallis finally broke through 20 minutes before lunch they had extended their partnership to 385.
Waugh was finally caught behind for 160 from 366 balls in 501 minutes with 22 fours. His 12th test century was also his seventh score over 150.

Blewett's innings is the highest ever made at the Wanderers, beating England captain Mike Atherton's 185 not out two years ago. He reached his 200 in 489 minutes from 377 balls with 32 fours and has so far batted for 513 minutes, receiving 417 balls with 34 fours.
It was the highest partnership against South Africa in their test history, beating the 370 for the third wicket of English pair Bill Edrich and Denis Compton at Lords in 1947.
Along the way it passed the previous highest Australian stand for any wicket against South Africa, beating the 275 for the fifth wicket by Colin McDonald and Lindsay Hassett in Adelaide in 1952/53.

On a pitch showing few signs of wear Mark Taylor will need to judge his declaration carefully. The last two tests on this ground have been saved by sides batting through the final day with little discomfort.
